svg.text: Mission plan editor — the task form, the 'then' picker, phases, the Tasks timeline (house style; design §5)
Annotations in grey are not drawn by the app.
A · A task in the Orders tab — an order first, then a plain 'then', an optional give-up
Move to grid 3412, then when there
Hold at the crossroads, then when Phase 2 begins
then the task is Failed and the plan goes on
B · Operation phases — triggers marked as phases, in the Rules window
when OBJ BLUE held · latest H+20
when all of 1st Platoon finish task 3
A phase IS a trigger (D5): begins = fires; Begin now = Fire (instructor, Live);
'no later than' = its when OR scenario time ≥ H+20.
C · The Timeline's Tasks group — ONE lane for all units, bars for the selection (E4)
Bravo 1-1 · task 2 Overwatch · Failed (gave up after 10 min)
ONE Tasks lane for every unit (E4, R-4161 — thousands of units stay one row): a marker per task start / Done / Failed, hover names unit and task;
it follows the timeline's entity filter. The SELECTED unit also shows its own tasks as bars. Phase triggers' fire times are the violet columns; the playhead is red.
D · Advanced condition… — WHO is 'this unit' by default, never an empty field (E5)
The chip is a real choice: another unit, a rule or a phase; stored with no OnEntity wrapper.
A Wait task (E9) has no order: its 'then' is required; an empty 'then' elsewhere means 'when done'.
when a unit finishes a task ▸
